name: Lin Zhenhua
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Sichuan Kexin Mechanical and Electrical Equipment Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 300092)
profile: Lin Zhenhua (林祯华) chairs Sichuan Kexin Mechanical & Electrical, a Shenzhen-listed maker of large heavy-duty pressure vessels and process equipment for nuclear power, new energy, petrochemical and coal/gas chemical plants. He is its largest individual shareholder (~15.6%), with Lin Zhenrong holding a similar stake; re-elected to the board in 2020.
interesting_fact: Kexin's heavy pressure vessels are supplied into nuclear power and new-energy projects, putting a Sichuan family-run equipment maker in the energy-infrastructure supply chain.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an MBA from Sichuan University and has also been a director of Sichuan Sunshine Plastics since 2007.
notes: Very low public profile; no English bio. Best route is likely the company's board secretary (董秘) contact listed in Kexin's annual report on cninfo.com.cn; company website could not be loaded. Wealth shared with Lin Zhenfu / Lin Zhenrong.

name: Ajit S Shriram
current_role: Joint Managing Director, DCM Shriram Ltd.
profile: Ajit S. Shriram is the youngest of three brothers (with Ajay and Vikram Shriram) running DCM Shriram, the Delhi-based conglomerate spun out of the old DCM Group in 1990, spanning chlor-alkali chemicals, sugar, fertilisers, Bioseed, Fenesta windows and PVC. He has served on the board for about two decades.
interesting_fact: He is a past President of the Indian Sugar Mills Association (ISMA) and a member of the CII National Council on Agriculture.
deep_cut_fact: After a commerce degree from Osmania University, Hyderabad, he did his MBA at IMD Lausanne; his company bio lists his passions as travel, photography and theatre.
notes: Press email is the published Corporate Communication/CSR contact (Ms. Aman Pannu). Energy angle: DCM Shriram is a large captive power and chlor-alkali (energy-intensive) operator.

name: Aroon Purie
current_role: Chairman & Editor-in-Chief, India Today Group; Chairman & MD, TV Today Network
profile: Aroon Purie (b. 1944) is the founder-publisher and editor-in-chief of India Today, launched in 1975, and built the India Today Group into a diversified media house (Aaj Tak, India Today TV, magazines, radio, printing via Thomson Press). In 2017 he passed day-to-day control to daughter Kalli Purie but remains editor-in-chief.
interesting_fact: Awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2001; in 2025 at FICCI Frames he warned AI poses an 'existential threat' to credible journalism.
deep_cut_fact: A chartered accountant and LSE economics graduate (1965), he began his career in 1970 as a production controller at the family's Thomson Press printing business; he was a Doon School contemporary of Rajiv Gandhi.
notes: No published personal or press email found; route via India Today Group corporate office/editorial. Media figure rather than energy; AI-in-media views may be a hook.

name: Venugopal Dhoot
current_role: Former Chairman, Videocon Group (company taken over in insolvency)
profile: Venugopal Dhoot built Videocon from a colour-TV maker launched with his father Nandlal Dhoot into a consumer-durables, DTH, telecom and oil & gas conglomerate, appearing on Forbes lists 2007-2015. Videocon Industries went into insolvency and was taken over; he no longer runs an operating business.
interesting_fact: Videocon started by making colour televisions in India and grew into one of the country's best-known consumer electronics brands, later expanding into oil & gas exploration (Brazil, Mozambique stakes).
notes: Not recommended: subject of ongoing ICICI loan case (arrested Dec 2022, on bail) and personal insolvency proceedings upheld by NCLAT in 2026. No published contact route found.

name: Sankar Sen
profile: Shankar (Sankar/Shaankar) Sen, founder chairman and MD of Kolkata jeweller Senco Gold, died on 28 July 2020. His son Suvankar Sen now leads the company as MD & CEO.
notes: Deceased 28 July 2020 (source: indianjeweller.in obituary). Successor at Senco Gold: Suvankar Sen.

name: Daniel Masters
current_role: Co-founder and Non-executive Director (former Executive Chairman), CoinShares
profile: Daniel Masters (b. 1963) is a veteran energy trader turned crypto pioneer. After heading global energy trading at Morgan Guaranty Trust and working in Salomon's energy division, he founded Jersey-based commodities manager Global Advisors, launched the world's first regulated bitcoin fund (GABI) in 2014, and co-founded CoinShares, now a Nasdaq-listed digital-asset manager.
interesting_fact: He launched GABI, described as the world's first regulated bitcoin fund, out of Jersey in 2014 - years before institutional crypto ETPs.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto he helped establish the UK's natural gas and electricity markets, completed some of the first forward contracts for electricity, and was among the earliest active traders in European Contracts for Difference.
notes: Excellent energy+crypto fit: physics graduate (Exeter), MSc OR (Imperial), 30+ years in energy trading. Route via CoinShares press office.

name: Stephen Trundle
current_role: President & CEO and Director, Alarm.com Holdings (Nasdaq: ALRM)
profile: Steve Trundle has run Alarm.com since 2003, after serving as a technology executive (CTO) at MicroStrategy, where Alarm.com began as an R&D spinoff in 2000. He led it through a 2009 management buyout and a 2015 IPO; it is now a large cloud platform for connected security, video and smart-home/energy management.
interesting_fact: Alarm.com bought demand-response/DERMS firm EnergyHub in 2013, now a grid-flexibility platform for utilities - a direct link to the energy/grid theme.
deep_cut_fact: Alarm.com was one of dozens of premium domains Michael Saylor bought for ~$2M at MicroStrategy; at the 2009 buyout ($27.7M) Trundle's company had about 150,000 customers sold through ~800 dealers. Trundle holds a Dartmouth degree in engineering sciences and government.
